title: Weight-Space Programming compiles facts into sparse concept tables without gradient training
summary: POSTECH EffL researchers demonstrate that language models writing weights directly compile knowledge into sparse concept tables instead of standard transformers, yielding up to ~1,800x parameter reduction and higher GPU inference throughput while underperforming gradient descent on continuous perceptual tasks.
research_notes:
Clone the repository and install required environment dependencies: git clone https://github.com/effl-lab/Weight-Space-Programming.git

Define target task specifications, few-shot demonstrations, and configure the local interactive execution sandbox.

Prompt a frontier reasoning language model to extract concepts and compile key-value weights and fixed search routines without backpropagation.

Evaluate the generated sparse concept table on target reasoning benchmarks and inspect row-level activations for error analysis.

Constrain weight-space compilation to sparse associative concept tables rather than attempting to hand-code dense multi-layer transformer matrices.

Deploy weight-space synthesis specifically for reasoning and structured knowledge retrieval tasks where human-written facts can be isolated, avoiding raw perceptual pixel tasks where gradient descent remains superior.

Utilize the tabular row-based representation of compiled weights for line-by-line inspection and surgical parameter debugging without risking catastrophic forgetting or global parameter drift.
